scope: Reconcile current open-source DXF/DWG string and renderer observations with the official target-version text contract and local text-codec coverage; refine existing implementation owners without asserting peer defects locally or promoting support.

method.kind: Primary documentation and issue/release review plus targeted local source/test audit
localInspection: asciiHex() accepts both upper- and lower-case ASCII hexadecimal digits; the conversion path uses hexadecimal parsing.
testMifEscapePolicy() contains lower-case MIF hex controls, while no explicit lower-case CIF \U+abcd positive was found in the inspected test corpus.
The existing local zero-height MTEXT test asserts explicit zero-value presence but does not exercise a rendering backend.
Existing PAR-05/7AR, PAR-19/29, PAR-22/7H/7I/7AB and composed consumer owners already cover the relevant route families; no new PAR finding or top-level subplan is required.
method.evidenceRule: Official Autodesk DXF documentation constrains target-version string serialization. Peer issues and release notes provide version-scoped test leads only; they are not local reproductions, general format rules, or support qualification.

evidence.topic: DXF string encoding is selected by target version
evidence.observed: Autodesk's group-code reference documents plain ASCII and CIF for pre-R2007 DXF output and UTF-8 for R2007 and later. Its examples show Unicode control sequences but do not define how every arbitrary application/object string containing a backslash escape must be interpreted.
evidence.planUse: Keep source-DWG decoding separate from target-DXF serialization. For text controls, assert physical emitted bytes, declared target version, semantic scalar and strict UTF-8 validity independently. Keep MTEXT inline controls distinct from generic/XRECORD string payloads until field semantics are established.

evidence.topic: Source DWG TV/TU path may affect Unicode escape output
evidence.observed: The open report describes different handling of stored \U+XXXX sequences through pre-R2007 TV and R2007+ TU source paths when targeting the same modern DXF version. The author reports a 43-file patch comparison, but frames intended behavior as unresolved; the peer patch and measurements were not independently reproduced.
doesNotEstablish: the required interpretation of every backslash-U sequence in every DXF string field
that the author's patch or file corpus is a normative oracle
evidence.planUse: Retain the existing source-storage-path × target-version matrix under PAR-05/7AR. Use locally generated controls, inspect raw DXF tags and semantic output separately, and avoid globally expanding every escape substring. Include BMP and lone-surrogate negatives in the existing focused codec/text targets.

evidence.topic: Lower-case CIF/MIF hex is a useful fast compatibility sentinel
evidence.observed: ezdxf 1.4.4 records a fix for lower-case hexadecimal digits in CIF/MIF strings. Local source inspection shows ASCII hex classification and numeric conversion accept lower-case; current tests explicitly cover lower-case MIF but not a lower-case CIF positive. This is a test-coverage gap, not a reproduced parser defect. PyPI lists ezdxf 1.4.5 released on 2026-10-16; the 1.4.4 release note is historical evidence, not a 1.4.5 runtime result.
evidence.planUse: Add one lowercase \U+abcd -> U+ABCD scalar control and suffix-consumption assertion to the existing codec test owner. Do not add a new CTest or production code absent a failing vector. Pin the exact 1.4.5 package/runtime if a later composed peer comparison uses ezdxf.

evidence.topic: Text rendering hazards are not file-parser failures
evidence.observed: The ezdxf 1.4.4 release notes identify fixes for rendering zero-height TEXT/MTEXT without an infinite loop and for clipping-depth handling. Local libdxfrw does not render drawings; existing zero-height MTEXT coverage observes input presence/value only.
evidence.planUse: Preserve parser/writer value and presence behavior independently of rendering. If rendering is in an existing composed consumer checkpoint, isolate a zero-height case with a bounded timeout and keep clipping recursion with the renderer that owns it. Do not add renderer work or full-suite runs per format slice.

evidence.topic: Whole-file AC1032 MTEXT rejection remains under-specified
evidence.observed: The reporter distinguishes frame-only flag 90=16 from 17 and reports version-dependent AutoCAD acceptance, but notes that matching the MTEXT object bytes did not make the whole AC1032 file open. Omitted VisualStyle/detail-view objects are a hypothesis only.
evidence.planUse: Keep the existing PAR-19/29 and 7D/7E/7M field/version controls. Do not rewrite flag values or synthesize unrelated objects from this report. Any future whole-file writer change needs exact output-version, complete object-root inventory and application audit in addition to entity-byte assertions.

evidence.topic: Reported DWG-to-DXF spline failure lacks an independently established curve case
evidence.observed: The report describes a GDAL GeoJSON conversion failure but does not provide structured offending spline arrays or an independently verified expected curve in its issue text; its linked explanation is an AI chat.
evidence.planUse: Continue the existing spline owner using exact source/emitted control points, knots and weights plus an analytic curve point and exact consumer diagnostics. Do not infer a format rule from that report or use generic conversion success as semantic proof.

planImpact.fastNextAction: Add one lower-case CIF scalar and following-text control to the existing codec test owner, run only its strict focused target, then continue the current implementation queue.
planImpact.qualificationBoundary: No peer/native runtime or full test suite was run. Renderer tests remain optional and composed-only.
